katas.title: Index rebuild: flip to the new generation as soon as the snapshot is loaded

seededDefectKey.scenario: A ticket is renamed while a REBUILD job is loading its snapshot; the incremental job indexes the rename before the flip.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The rename was written into the old generation, which the flip deletes; the new generation holds the older snapshot title, and the cursor has already advanced past the event so no later incremental run replays it. The document stays stale until the entity changes again — finding T4, reintroduced by trusting the snapshot alone.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shipped incremental runner always writes to the active generation while the rebuild flips and deletes it.
seededDefectKey.consequence: In production the same window exists today: incremental documents land in the generation that completeTenantRebuild + deleteGenerationDocuments (indexingJobRunner.ts:125-129) are about to drop, and nothing re-drains the events processed during the rebuild into the new generation.

tests.name: a change indexed during the rebuild survives the cutover (finding T4)
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryIndexStore({ sourceRows: [{ entityId: 'ticket-1', title: 'Printer offline' }], events: [{ id: 1, entityId: 'ticket-1', title: 'Printer offline' }], }); await mod.runIncrementalJob(store); const takeSnapshot = store.listSourceSnapshot.bind(store); store.listSourceSnapshot = async () => { const snapshot = await takeSnapshot(); store.sourceRows = [{ entityId: 'ticket-1', title: 'Printer back online' }]; store.events.push({ id: 2, entityId: 'ticket-1', title: 'Printer back online' }); await mod.runIncrementalJob(store); return snapshot; }; await mod.runRebuildJob(store, 2); assert.equal(store.state.activeGeneration, 2); assert.equal(store.searchActiveGeneration('back online').length, 1, 'the rename indexed during the rebuild vanished at cutover');

tests.name: a rebuild with no concurrent changes replaces the active generation completely
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryIndexStore({ sourceRows: [{ entityId: 'a', title: 'Alpha' }, { entityId: 'b', title: 'Beta' }], events: [], }); await mod.runRebuildJob(store, 2); assert.equal(store.state.activeGeneration, 2); assert.equal(store.searchActiveGeneration('').length, 2); assert.equal([...store.documents.keys()].every((key) => key.startsWith('2:')), true);

tests.name: incremental writes land in the active generation and advance the cursor
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryIndexStore({ sourceRows: [], events: [{ id: 1, entityId: 'x', title: 'First' }] }); await mod.runIncrementalJob(store); assert.equal(store.state.lastProcessedEventId, 1); assert.equal(store.searchActiveGeneration('First').length, 1); await mod.runIncrementalJob(store); assert.equal(store.state.lastProcessedEventId, 1);

katas.title: Job runner: drain the whole queue so no tenant waits for its own owner

seededDefectKey.scenario: An OWNER of tenant A calls POST /api/indexing-jobs/run-pending while tenants B and C have queued jobs.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Tenant A's owner executes other tenants' indexing jobs, and the response lists their job ids and statuses — cross-tenant execution plus metadata disclosure. This is finding T1: the one place where the README's "every query scopes by tenant" rule stops holding.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shipped repository query selects QUEUED jobs for every tenant.
seededDefectKey.consequence: listQueuedIndexingJobs(limit) has no tenantId condition and runPendingIndexingJobs passes only a limit, so any tenant OWNER who clicks run-pending drains every tenant's queue today. The fix the guide prescribes is to pass context.session.tenantId into this query.

tests.name: run-pending executes only the caller's tenant's queued jobs (finding T1)
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryJobStore([ { id: 'job-a', tenantId: 'tenant-a' }, { id: 'job-b', tenantId: 'tenant-b' }, ]); const out = await mod.runPendingIndexingJobs(store, { session: { tenantId: 'tenant-a', tenantRole: 'OWNER' } }, { limit: 10 }); assert.equal(out.processed, 1); assert.deepEqual(store.executed, ['job-a']); assert.equal(out.results.some((r) => r.jobId === 'job-b'), false, 'another tenant\'s job id leaked into the response'); assert.equal(store.jobs.find((j) => j.id === 'job-b').status, 'QUEUED');

tests.name: a MEMBER cannot run pending jobs
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryJobStore([{ id: 'job-a', tenantId: 'tenant-a' }]); await assert.rejects(() => mod.runPendingIndexingJobs(store, { session: { tenantId: 'tenant-a', tenantRole: 'MEMBER' } }, { limit: 10 }), /FORBIDDEN/); assert.deepEqual(store.executed, []);

tests.name: a failing job is marked FAILED and the rest still complete
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryJobStore([ { id: 'j1', tenantId: 't1', payload: { poison: true } }, { id: 'j2', tenantId: 't1' }, ]); const out = await mod.runPendingIndexingJobs(store, { session: { tenantId: 't1', tenantRole: 'OWNER' } }, { limit: 10 }); assert.equal(out.processed, 2); assert.equal(store.jobs.find((j) => j.id === 'j1').status, 'FAILED'); assert.equal(store.jobs.find((j) => j.id === 'j1').error, 'index write failed'); assert.equal(store.jobs.find((j) => j.id === 'j2').status, 'COMPLETED');
